source.title: Retrieval is Enough: Training-Free Interpretability with a Tool-Using Agent

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE dictionary features can recover specified concepts in a Gemma LLM, an LLM setting rather than the original toy-model setting. It does not test superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The Concept10 detection experiment measures classification using the SAE feature associated with each concept. The paper also compares SAE-based concept discovery with HARP, but gives those scores only in Figure 2; the text reports that HARP outperforms the SAE without providing individual SAE values. It does not measure feature overlap, sparsity-dependent geometry, neuron polysemanticity, or feature dimensionality.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks its own retrieval agent (HARP) against an off-the-shelf Gemma-Scope SAE and an activation oracle on concept discovery, detection, steering and secret elicitation. The SAE serves only as a comparison baseline. Nothing is measured about superposition: no feature overlap, sparsity transitions, polysemantic neurons, capacity, spreading across neurons, or feature dimensionality. The SAE detection AUC also scores how well a feature labelled after a concept detects AxBench examples built from that same label. It does not test whether sparse features exist or are recoverable, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude HARP matches or beats SAEs and activation oracles on most tasks; the oracle wins on secret elicitation (80% vs 73%). They argue current training-based methods do not yet extract insights beyond what retrieval over their training data recovers. They also call for benchmarks requiring such insights.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce or apply the original toy-model superposition method; it evaluates an agentic retrieval system and SAE-based interpretation on Gemma.

fits_no_version.finding: As concept detectors, Gemma-Scope SAE features (labelled after the concepts) reach mean AUC 0.704 (all negatives) and 0.693 (hard negatives). A retrieval-built difference-of-means probe reaches 0.892 and 0.856. SAE features used as steering directions score 0.02 LM-judge vs 0.20 for HARP, with concept relevance 0.42 vs 0.78.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Off-the-shelf SAE features are weaker concept detectors and steering directions than simple linear probes built from retrieved examples (usefulness of SAE features, not superposition).

record.problems: The claim-relevant SAE detection evaluation covers 10 concepts on one model and layer. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the AUC results, and the SAE is evaluated using the feature labels that define the benchmark concepts.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 reports SAE-based concept-discovery results for Bills and Wiki, but supplies values only in the figure; the text states that HARP outperforms the SAE without giving separate SAE values for the metrics and conditions.

untested.parts: No toy models, overlap geometry or sparsity transitions.
Does not measure features spread across neurons. Does not test whether an SAE recovers sparse features; it only scores a pretrained SAE's features as concept detectors against other methods.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features. Related work on non-canonical units is only cited.
Not tested. HARP's use of 3–5-dim subspaces for some concepts is a design choice, not a result about the model's features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/tests classification and its V4 labels are rejected. The SAE numbers are baseline scores in a method comparison, and the benchmark concepts derive from the SAE's own feature labels. The SAE steering results (Sec 3.2, App B.5) and the secret/gender elicitation results (51%, 72%) are likewise method-comparison values with no bearing on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overlapping near-orthogonal feature directions, sparsity transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
Does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemantic neurons or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE-feature detection for 10 concepts on one Gemma model; does not measure feature spreading across neurons or establish general recovery across models and tasks.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: google/gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Scores examples using the maximum sequence activation of the SAE feature whose label defines each concept.
rows.measure: ROC-AUC, positive versus random and hard negatives
rows.note: The SAE is given the feature whose auto-interpretation label defines each evaluated concept; the paper describes this as an oracle setting for the SAE. The authors report that it lags behind HARP and the activation oracle.
rows.check: Baseline score of an SAE feature in the authors' method comparison (SAE 0.704 vs HARP 0.892, oracle 0.877). Concepts are defined by the SAE's own auto-interp labels, so this cannot show whether a dictionary recovers model features (V4). State 'observed' has no version effect to attach to.

rows.subject: google/gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Scores examples using the maximum sequence activation of the SAE feature whose label defines each concept.
rows.note: The hard negatives are topically related examples that avoid the target concept. The authors report that the SAE lags well behind HARP and the activation oracle.
rows.check: Same as r1, but against hard negatives only (SAE 0.693 vs HARP 0.856, oracle 0.756). This is a method-comparison value, not a measure of superposition or feature recovery. The 'partial' state is not grounded in any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Concept10 detection with random and hard negatives
reader_labels.reason: The SAE feature associated with each concept yields a reported mean AUC of 0.704, showing concept-detection performance in this tested setting (r1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported mean AUC is 0.693, and the authors say SAE performance lags the other methods, limiting the strength of this recovery evidence for closely related confounders (r2).
